comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, AMD had approximately 28,000 employees in its global workforce.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD disclose their total global employee headcount as of the end of fiscal 2024. Qualcomm reported approximately 49,000 employees, while AMD reported approximately 28,000 employees. Both companies characterize their workforces as having a significant engineering or technical focus, with Qualcomm noting the 'substantial majority' work in engineering/technical roles and AMD providing general headcount data in the same human capital context.

comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal year 2024, the company's global voluntary attrition rate was approximately 2.9% (excluding VMware merger employees) and 6.2% (including them), both below the technology industry benchmark from AON's 2024 study.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Broadcom report their voluntary turnover/attrition rates for fiscal 2024, providing a direct comparison of employee retention metrics. Qualcomm reported a voluntary turnover rate of approximately 5%, whereas Broadcom reported a lower global voluntary attrition rate of approximately 2.9% (excluding VMware merger employees) and 6.2% (including them). This highlights different retention outcomes within the same industry timeframe.

sentences.text: During fiscal 2024, our voluntary turnover rate was approximately 5%.

Our global voluntary attrition rates in fiscal year 2024 were approximately 2.9% (excluding employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger) and approximately 6.2% (including employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger), which are both below the technology industry benchmark (AON, 2024 Salary Increase and Turnover Study - Second Edition, September 2024).

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces significant competition for talent and limited hiring in 2024, with headcount actions expected to decrease the core workforce by approximately 15% by early 2025. Undesired turnover rates were 5.9% in 2024 and 5.6% in 2023.

Intel reported an 'undesired turnover rate' of 5.9%, noting that this metric specifically includes all regular employees who voluntarily left but excludes various separations like retirement or divestiture. The rates are comparable in magnitude, though Intel's metric definition is more restrictive.
